# opencode-router **Per-turn model routing for OpenCode V2 and Kilo.** A small model running on your machine picks the right model for every turn — so a one-line question doesn't cost frontier tokens, and a hard refactor doesn't run on a model that will fail it. [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@231self/opencode-router?color=3b82f6&label=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@231self/opencode-router) [![ci](https://github.com/231self/opencode-router/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/231self/opencode-router/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-22c55e)](LICENSE) [![node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%E2%89%A522-111827)](https://nodejs.org)
> **Status: v0.2.8.** Routing, the context optimiser, subagent policy, the TUI > `/router` surface, per-turn timing, the CLI, and the Kilo shim are implemented > and tested. Design of record: > [`docs/specs/2026-11-15-opencode-omlx-router-design.md`](docs/specs/2026-11-15-opencode-omlx-router-design.md). ## Why A coding agent makes you pick one model for a whole session. A one-line question then costs frontier-model tokens, while a hard refactor on a small model burns retries. This plugin routes **each turn** to the model that fits it, from a pool you control. It ports the transferable ideas from [`pi-smart-router`](https://github.com/beettlle/pi-smart-router) — turn envelope, deterministic triage, context-fit gate, cache-aware pinning, loop escalation, decision logging — and drops the heavy machinery (HyDRA/ONNX embeddings, benchmark calibration, virtual cost, planning delegate). The pool can mix cloud models with local oMLX or llama.cpp models. Loopback providers are priced at zero, so a capable local model can take routine turns while cloud models handle the hard ones. ## Quick start ```sh # 1. install opencode plugin add @231self/opencode-router # 2. choose the models the router may pick from opencode-model-router config set pool.source list opencode-model-router config set pool.models '["deepseek/deepseek-flash","deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"]' # 3. make sure a small judge model is served locally opencode-model-router judge probe # 4. talk normally; inspect the first decisions opencode-model-router status opencode-model-router history 5 ``` In the TUI, `/router` opens the full menu, `/router explain` shows why the last turn picked its model, and `/router debug` prints the diagnostic bundle. ## Documentation - [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) — adapter, WASM core, turn flow, subagents, pinning, optimiser. - [WASM protocol](docs/protocol.md) — ABI, request/response JSON, need-judge flow, optimiser plans. - [Configuration reference](docs/configuration.md) — every key, defaults, examples. - [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md) — symptoms, evidence, reset. - [Building and releasing](docs/releasing.md) — build, pack, publish, tag, consumer install. - [Benchmarks](docs/benchmarks/) — routing/cost suites and the live quality eval. - [Design spec](docs/specs/2026-11-15-opencode-omlx-router-design.md) and [implementation plan](docs/plans/2026-11-15-implementation.md). - [Development notes](docs/development.md) — probe results, verification, limits. ## Requirements | Requirement | Notes | |---|---| | [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) ≥ 2.3 | First-class; V2 plugin API | | [Kilo CLI](https://kilo.ai) ≥ 7.6.2 | Best-effort mode; see [Kilo limitations](#kilo-limitations) | | [oMLX](https://github.com/jundot/omlx) or [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp) | Local OpenAI-compatible server; oMLX defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1`, `llama-server` to `:8080` | | A small judge model | e.g. a ~4B instruct model; oMLX, llama.cpp, or any OpenAI-compatible server; see [Choose a judge](#choose-a-judge) | | Node/Bun | Provided by OpenCode and Kilo; nothing extra to install | No Rust toolchain is needed to install a released package. Building from source requires Rust with the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target. ## Install Release/build details: [docs/releasing.md](docs/releasing.md). ### OpenCode V2 ```sh opencode plugin add @231self/opencode-router ``` ```jsonc // ~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "plugins": ["@231self/opencode-router"] } ``` ### Kilo ```sh kilo plugin @231self/opencode-router ``` ```jsonc // ~/.config/kilo/kilo.jsonc or project kilo.jsonc { "$schema": "https://app.kilo.ai/config.json", "plugin": ["@231self/opencode-router"] } ``` ### From a checkout (development) ```sh git clone https://github.com/231self/opencode-router cd opencode-router bun install bun run build:wasm # needs Rust with wasm32-unknown-unknown ``` Then point the host at the checkout: ```jsonc // OpenCode { "plugins": ["/absolute/path/to/opencode-router"] } ``` ```jsonc // Kilo { "plugin": ["/absolute/path/to/opencode-router/src/index.js"] } ``` Kilo applies a decision at the next request boundary; see [Kilo limitations](#kilo-limitations). The CLI installs as `opencode-model-router`. `omlx-router` remains an alias. Config, state, plugin IDs, and `OMLX_ROUTER_*` env vars keep their historical names, so existing setups keep working. ## How it works Three layers: a plain-JS adapter for the host, a Rust decision engine compiled to WebAssembly, and a short JSON-verdict call to a small local model. ```text prompt hook ├─ envelope: cheap Rust heuristics → signals + complexity hint ├─ short-circuit? (trivial · forced pin · escalation · empty pool) ├─ judge: 4B local model → JSON verdict [5 s budget] ├─ reconcile: judge + deterministic floor (judge can raise, never lower) ├─ gates → score → pin → chosen model └─ session.switchModel(...) + write pin + decision record context hook (same turn) ├─ optimiser: token estimate → prune plan → afterTokens └─ afterTokens feeds the next routing decision telemetry (after the turn) └─ turns.jsonl: routing/judge/core/switch time, tokens, cost ``` The routing brain is deterministic, has no I/O, and is unit-tested on its own. The only model call the plugin makes for a decision is the short verdict prompt to the judge endpoint you configure (localhost by default). If it is slow or down, deterministic heuristics take over and routing continues. ### The judge A classifier, not a chat model. It is asked one question per turn, and sees only: - the turn truncated to 1,200 characters, - token counts, image count, and tool-failure count, - the deterministic signals (code, error, planning, review), - the candidate table — context, tools, vision, price, local flag. It never sees the transcript, file contents, or tool output. | Input | Value | |---|---| | Temperature | `0` | | Max tokens | `220` | | Format | `response_format: json_object`, one repair retry | | Timeout | `judge.timeoutMs` (default 5 s) | It returns: ```json {"task":"edit","complexity":2,"needsTools":true,"needsVision":false, "contextNeed":"small","reasoningNeed":"medium","confidence":0.8} ``` **The judge is a floor-adder.** `reconcile` lets it raise complexity, reasoning, or context need, but never lower what the deterministic signals already proved. That is why a 4B that under-classifies a multi-file refactor cannot cause an under-route. `confidence` is recorded but does not steer selection. On timeout, HTTP, or parse failure the heuristic verdict is used, the decision log records `used: false`, and the turn continues. ### Signals and complexity Before any judge call, the envelope computes word-boundary-aware markers: | Signal | Trigger | |---|---| | `code` | code fences, source extensions, `cargo`/`bun`/`npm`/`git` | | `agentic` | implement, fix, refactor, migrate, debug, add, run, test, … | | `error_trace` | panic, traceback, exception, `error:`, exit code, … | | `planning` | plan, design, architect, approach, trade-off, spec | | `review` | review, audit, critique, security, look for bugs | | `trivial` | short, no signals, small prompt and context | | `multi_file` | ≥ 3 code files, or 2 across files | | `large_context` | estimated input over 60k tokens | | `repeated_failures` | 3+ consecutive identical tool failures | Complexity starts at 1 and adds a point per signal (clamped to 5), with planning and review floored at 3. Trivial turns skip the judge entirely. ### Scoring 1. **Gates.** Deprecated models, context fit (`input ≤ context × 0.9`), minimum context, required tools, and required vision are hard filters. 2. **Required quality.** Complexity maps to 0.25 / 0.40 / 0.55 / 0.75 / 0.90, plus 0.10 for high reasoning and 0.05 for planning or review, then the agent's quality floor. 3. **Quality estimate.** 45% price percentile, 25% parameter-size heuristic, 15% context percentile, 15% reasoning support. Overrides win; free local models default to 0.35. 4. **Expected cost.** Input plus expected output at the model's context tier, with a cache-read discount: the measured cache-hit share of the session's last turn when the pinned model served it (a fresh pin is priced cold), or `pin.cacheHitRatio` (0.8) when nothing is measured yet. 5. **Policy weights.** | Policy | Cost | Quality | Latency | Use when | |---|---:|---:|---:|---| | `cost` (default) | 0.6 | 0.3 | 0.1 | Cheapest model that clears the bar | | `quality` | 0.1 | 0.8 | 0.1 | Quality matters more than spend | | `latency` | 0.2 | 0.2 | 0.6 | Interactive work; favours local and flash tiers | Changing the policy clears pins so the next turn is scored from scratch. ### Custom weights Override any preset, and optionally vary the blend by turn class: ```jsonc { "policy": "cost", "policyWeights": { "cost": 0.6, "quality": 0.35, "latency": 0.05 }, "policyByClass": { "planning": { "cost": 0.1, "quality": 0.8, "latency": 0.1 }, "review": { "cost": 0.1, "quality": 0.8, "latency": 0.1 }, "trivial": { "cost": 0.85, "quality": 0.1, "latency": 0.05 } } } ``` Turn classes are `trivial`, `routine`, `agentic`, `planning`, `review`, and `tool_continuation`. A class override wins over `policyWeights`; omitted fields inherit. `/router policy custom` prints the active weights and the config path. Weights change which model wins a turn; pin thresholds decide whether the router switches at all. ### Pinning Provider prompt caches are per model and per provider. A switch pays one full prefill, so routing alone would thrash the cache. The pin is the counterweight. | Mode | Behaviour | |---|---| | `cache` | Keep the incumbent to reuse its cache; switch only on hard breaks | | `balanced` (default) | Keep unless a challenger wins by `pin.switchThreshold` (0.12) | | `switch` | Take the best every turn, with cold-cache scoring | Even in `cache` or `balanced`, a pin is released by: - idle TTL (`pin.idleTtlMs`, 5 min), - a complexity jump of two or more, - pin age (`pin.maxAgeMs`, 30 min) or pinned turns (`pin.maxTurns`, 8), - an incumbent costing over `pin.costSwitchRatio` (4×) the cheapest **adequate** challenger, - a flip-flop guard (`pin.flipFlopTurns`, 3), - a gate failure, context overflow, compaction, policy change, or user override. Picking a model yourself (`/model`) becomes a forced pin until you run `/router auto`, the session compacts, or the model disappears. ### Smaller context windows On OpenCode V2, before automatically switching to a model with less room, the router reads the active conversation and budgets for the new prompt, instructions, and output. If the preferred model would be too small, the router can queue one compaction while keeping the current model. A later user prompt must see a new, completed checkpoint and confirm the resulting context fits before switching. If the check fails or the summary is still too large, the router does not downgrade or keep re-requesting compaction. `limits.compactOnDowngrade: false` disables automatic compaction without disabling the fit check. ### Provider failover A 429, 5xx, timeout, auth, billing, or quota failure blocks the model for the session — 5 min for rate limits, 1 min for server errors, 5 min for auth and billing. Auth, payment, and quota failures block the whole provider; rate limits and server errors block the one model. The pin is cleared and the next candidate from the last decision is queued. OpenCode's `model.resolve` hook swaps it in on the retry; if the host never retries, the next turn routes around the blocked model. 400-class request errors are not treated as provider failures. The pool needs a second provider or model for a switch to happen. `/router pins` shows per-session blocks and pins, `/router debug` shows the active blocks, and `failover.enabled: false` restores plain host behaviour. ### Context optimiser When the assembled request fits, **nothing is changed** — cache-safe by construction. When it does not fit, the optimiser works in order and stops as soon as the request fits: 1. Deduplicate identical tool outputs, keeping the newest. 2. Truncate outputs above `optimiser.maxToolTokens` (2,000) to 60% head + 40% tail, with a marker. 3. Stub older tool outputs, largest first, keeping the last `keepRecentToolOutputs` (3). System instructions, user text, the first user message, recent turns, and error outputs are protected. If pruning cannot fit the request, the optimiser reports `overflow`, clears the pin, and lets OpenCode compact; the next turn routes to a model with a larger window. Compaction, title, and transient generation requests are never pruned or routed. ### The three caches These are unrelated and worth keeping apart: | Cache | Scope | Invalidation | |---|---|---| | Provider prompt cache | Per model/provider; Anthropic markers, OpenAI prefix, oMLX KV | Not portable across models; the pin protects it | | Judge verdict cache | In-process LRU, 128 entries, 10 min | Prompt fingerprint, agent, policy, pool, context tokens | | Host catalog | OpenCode refreshes models.dev (~15 min) and exposes it live | Plugin caches the catalog for 2 s, `/models` for 60 s | Pricing comes from the host catalog, so it follows models.dev automatically. Local models have no catalog price; set `providers..models..cost` if you want the cost policy to weigh them. ### Subagents Subagents route independently, with their own pins, so an `explore` subagent can run cheap and fast while the parent stays on a strong model. Detection is via the child session's `parentID`; the agent identity comes from the session metadata. Resolution order: 1. An explicit model configured on the agent (respected as a forced pin unless `subagents.overrideExplicitModel` is `true`). 2. `subagents.agents[agentID]`. 3. `subagents.default`. 4. The global policy. The shipped defaults: `explore` is latency-first with 128k minimum context, `general` is cost-first with a 0.55 floor, and `review`/`plan` are quality-first with high floors. Loop escalation is per session, so a failing subagent escalates itself without dragging the parent. On a score tie, a child prefers the parent's model to reuse its cache. ## Choose the pool The **pool** is the set of models the router may choose from. By default it uses your host favorites. You can instead name the models explicitly: ```sh opencode-model-router config set pool.source list opencode-model-router config set pool.models '["deepseek/deepseek-flash","deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"]' opencode-model-router config set pool.minContext 32000 ``` Or edit `~/.config/omlx-router/config.json`: ```jsonc { "pool": { "source": "list", "models": [ "deepseek/deepseek-flash", "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro" ], "requireTools": true, "minContext": 32000 } } ``` | Source | Behaviour | |---|---| | `favorites` | Models favorited in OpenCode/Kilo (default). Empty favorites mean **no pool**; routing pauses rather than silently using every model | | `list` | Exactly `pool.models` (use `provider/model#variant` for a variant) | | `available` | Every eligible chat model the host advertises (explicit opt-in) | An empty `favorites` pool does **not** fall back to all models. That prevents zero-cost or unintended models from being selected without your opt-in; set `source: "available"` if that is what you want. An unknown source selects …[文件过长——中段 8KB 抽样]… pseek/deepseek-v4-pro" ], "requireTools": true, "minContext": 32000 } } ``` | Source | Behaviour | |---|---| | `favorites` | Models favorited in OpenCode/Kilo (default). Empty favorites mean **no pool**; routing pauses rather than silently using every model | | `list` | Exactly `pool.models` (use `provider/model#variant` for a variant) | | `available` | Every eligible chat model the host advertises (explicit opt-in) | An empty `favorites` pool does **not** fall back to all models. That prevents zero-cost or unintended models from being selected without your opt-in; set `source: "available"` if that is what you want. An unknown source selects nothing and reports a warning. The TUI tells you when the pool is empty: at startup and in `/router status` it points to `/router pool`, which offers **Use my favorites**, **Enter an explicit list**, or **Use all available**. `pool.include` / `pool.exclude` add or drop globs after the source; `maxModels` caps the judge's candidate table; `requireTools` and `minContext` are hard filters. `/router pool` (or `opencode-model-router pool`) shows the resolved pool, the config path, and the exact commands to change it. If model names do not contain parameter sizes (for example `deepseek-flash` and `deepseek-v4-pro`), set explicit quality scores so the quality floor can distinguish them: ```jsonc { "quality": { "overrides": { "deepseek/deepseek-flash": 0.55, "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro": 0.8 } } } ``` Quality is `0..1`; the router uses it with complexity/reasoning requirements. Without overrides it falls back to price, context, name-size, and reasoning heuristics. ## Choose a judge The judge is a small instruct model served by a local OpenAI-compatible server (oMLX, llama.cpp, or similar). It answers one short JSON question per turn: how complex is this turn, does it need tools/vision/long context, how much reasoning, and how confident is it. A ~4B model is the sweet spot: fast enough for a per-turn hop, reliable enough for structured output. Recommended: a Qwen3-4B-class MLX instruct model, pulled through the oMLX app's model browser. A 1.7B-class model works for coarse classification; a 27B model works but adds real prefill cost to every turn. The plugin defaults to `judge.model: "auto"`, which picks the smallest model the `/v1/models` endpoint advertises. Set it explicitly if you run several small models: ```json { "judge": { "model": "Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-4bit" } } ``` ### Pull the judge from the plugin (with consent) The plugin can ask oMLX to download the recommended judge. It **never downloads without an explicit confirmation**: you see the repository, parameter count, download size, license, and source first. ```text /router judge # offers the download when no suitable judge exists /router judge pull [repo] # explicit pull, same confirmation /router judge status # progress /router judge cancel [task] # cancel an active download ``` ```sh opencode-model-router judge pull # prints the summary, asks y/N opencode-model-router judge pull --yes # skips only the prompt opencode-model-router judge pull mlx-community/Some-Other-4B opencode-model-router judge status opencode-model-router judge cancel ``` The download uses oMLX's own admin API and its Hugging Face downloader, so the model lands in oMLX's model directory and is discovered when complete. It needs the oMLX **main** API key (sub-keys cannot administer downloads): ```jsonc { "judge": { "provision": { "adminApiKey": "{env:OMLX_ADMIN_API_KEY}", "readSettingsKey": true, "repo": "mlx-community/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-4bit" } } } ``` If `adminApiKey` is unset, the plugin falls back to `auth.api_key` in `~/.omlx/settings.json` when `readSettingsKey` is true. The key is only used for the local admin login, never logged, and the session cookie stays in memory. Non-MLX repositories are rejected unless `allowNonMlx` is set. Verify with: ```text /router judge ``` This prints the selected model, a sample verdict, and the round-trip latency. ### Using llama.cpp or another server The verdict path is plain OpenAI-compatible: `GET /v1/models` and `POST /v1/chat/completions`, an optional Bearer key, and `response_format` with a fallback for servers that reject it. Point `judge.baseURL` at any such server. ```sh llama-server -m Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-Q4_K_M.gguf --port 8080 ``` ```jsonc { "judge": { "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1", "model": "auto", // or the alias llama-server reports "provision": { "backend": "none" } // optional; auto-detected anyway } } ``` The download helper (`judge pull`, `judge status`, `judge cancel`) uses the oMLX admin API. On any other endpoint the plugin detects that and prints the setup recipe instead of failing. Routing, pinning, the optimiser, and timing are backend-agnostic. ## Route to local models Add the server as an OpenAI-compatible provider in the host, then include its models in the pool. oMLX on `:1234` and llama.cpp on `:8080` both work: ```jsonc "providers": { "omlx": { "package": "@opencode/ai/providers/openai-compatible", "settings": { "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1" }, "models": { "Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-4bit": { "capabilities": { "tools": true } } } } } ``` The router detects loopback providers, prices them at zero (`pool.localCostZero`), and gives them a size-based quality: under 3B 0.35, 3–8B 0.45, 8–30B 0.55, 30B+ 0.72. An 8k-token routine edit no longer counts as hard work, so a local 27B can take those turns. Oversized local models still lose to cloud models when the turn requires more; set `quality.overrides` when you have a real measurement. ## Quality scores Quality comes from two public datasets by default, with no API key: 1. **Epoch AI** — SWE-bench Verified or MirrorCode when the model is tracked, otherwise the Epoch Capabilities Index (ECI). 2. **LMArena** — the Code Arena (`webdev`) leaderboard. Both are fetched from public endpoints, normalised into the same 0.35–0.97 band, and cached for 24 hours at `~/.local/state/omlx-router/quality.json`. Source priority is configurable. `quality.overrides` always win; unmatched models keep the heuristic or the local size tier. ```jsonc { "quality": { "source": "auto", // auto | epoch | lmarena | manual "sources": ["epoch", "lmarena"], // first match wins "refreshHours": 24 } } ``` ```sh opencode-model-router quality refresh # fetch now opencode-model-router quality status # per-source counts and age ``` In the TUI: `/router quality` and `/router quality refresh`. `/router pool` shows the score and its source for each model. Set `"quality": { "source": "manual" }` to turn the fetch off. Epoch AI data is [CC-BY](https://epoch.ai/benchmarks/use-this-data); LMArena is [CC-BY-4.0](https://huggingface.co/datasets/lmarena-ai/leaderboard-dataset). Attribution to both is kept here. ## Pricing A model's price is read from the host catalog first, then from public price tables when the catalog has none. OpenCode reports `cost: []` for some providers and all-zero prices for others; those used to show as `$0`, and a partially reported price used to zero out the missing field. Missing prices now read as `unknown`, and the router fills real gaps from: 1. **models.dev** — the same catalogue OpenCode reads, flat per-million prices. 2. **LiteLLM** — per-token costs converted to per million. Neither needs an access token. Only missing or zero fields are filled, so first-party billing still wins when the host reports it. The merged table is cached for 24 hours at `~/.local/state/omlx-router/pricing.json`. ```jsonc { "pricing": { "source": "modelsdev", // modelsdev | off "sources": ["modelsdev", "litellm"], // first source wins per model "refreshHours": 24 } } ``` ```sh opencode-model-router pricing refresh opencode-model-router pricing anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 ``` In the TUI: `/router pricing` lists each pool model with its source, and `/router pricing refresh` …[仅保留首 16KB/中段 8KB/末 8KB]… or clear | | `/router history [n]` | Recent decisions, including subagents and judge/route time | | `/router timing [n]` | Local judge vs remote model vs tool time per turn | | `/router explain` | Readable why: chosen model, policy, verdict, top scores, and per-turn costs | | `/router pin` / `/router auto` | Force or release a model pin for this session | | `/router judge` | Probe the judge: model, latency, sample verdict | | `/router subagents on\|off` | Toggle subagent routing | | `/router help [command]` | Command reference; name one command to see its options | Commands that take optional parameters print a `usage:` line naming them, and an unknown parameter is rejected with the allowed values rather than ignored. A command that needs a subcommand and is run bare shows that command's help rather than guessing. `pin` (force one session) and `pins` (per-session state) are about a single session; `retention` is the strategy that decides how eagerly the router leaves a model. The old `pin-mode` name is an alias of `retention`. **Everything is reachable from `/router`.** The menu lists every command above, including the routing toggle, the `pricing refresh`, `quality refresh`, and `pins clear` subcommands, and Help — which opens a picker of commands and shows the options for the one you pick. `/router help ` does the same from the prompt. **Routing is on by default.** `/router status` shows `state enabled` or `state disabled`; `/router on` and `/router off` gate routing entirely. If status says `enabled` and the model still never changes, routing is working and keeping the incumbent — `/router explain` shows whether the last turn was `forced` (a manual model choice the router honors), `pin-kept` (the challenger was not better by enough), or `first-turn` (the pin expired and the same model won again). Menu items have descriptions and are navigable with the arrow keys, Enter, and Esc. A palette entry, **"OpenCode Router: settings"**, opens the same menu without typing a command. When routing changes the model, the plugin refreshes the session and shows a short `model → …` toast; the host footer follows the session model. ### CLI Works in any host, including Kilo, headless OpenCode, and CI: ```sh opencode-model-router status opencode-model-router version [--json] opencode-model-router debug [--json] opencode-model-router doctor opencode-model-router pool opencode-model-router pricing [refresh|provider/model] opencode-model-router history 20 opencode-model-router timing 20 opencode-model-router config get policy opencode-model-router config set policy quality ``` `version` prints the bare version for scripts; `version --json` adds the package name, ABI, host, and wasm path. `debug` is read-only and never prints secrets. ## Kilo limitations Kilo 7.6.2 uses the V1 plugin API, which has no per-request model hook. The shim switches the session model at the next request boundary; a decision therefore applies to the following turn, and the decision log records `applied: "boundary"`. If Kilo's model-switching API is unavailable to plugins, the shim reports `kilo: unsupported` and stays out of the way rather than pretending to route. Kilo has no `/router` command and no TUI settings dialog; use the `opencode-model-router` CLI and `config.json`. ## Privacy - Decision and turn records store **no prompt, message, or tool-output text** — only signals, model ids, scores, timings, token counts, cost, and a hashed session id. - The only text that leaves the machine is the truncated turn summary in the judge request, sent to the `judge.baseURL` you configure (localhost by default). - When quality scores are enabled, the plugin fetches public datasets from Epoch AI and Hugging Face (LMArena). Those requests contain no prompts, files, or local paths; set `quality.source` to `manual` to disable them. - API keys are read from your config/env and never logged. The oMLX admin key may be read from the local `~/.omlx/settings.json` (when allowed) solely for the local download login. - `opencode-model-router debug` prints a secret-free config digest, never key values. - State is local: `~/.local/state/omlx-router//`. ## Troubleshooting | Symptom | Check | |---|---| | Routing does nothing | `/router status`: `state enabled`? empty pool? judge errors? | | Model never changes | `/router status` says `enabled`, so routing is keeping the incumbent: `/router explain` reads `forced`, `pin-kept`, or `first-turn`; `/router policy quality` stops cost-first favouring a free model | | Forgot a subcommand | `/router help `, or `/router` → Help → pick the command | | Judge timeouts | `/router judge`; raise `judge.timeoutMs`, use a smaller judge model | | Wrong model chosen | `/router explain`; adjust `quality.overrides`, policy, or pool | | Model switching visibly lags | Kilo boundary behaviour, or a host that rejects the switch; check the decision log | | Context overflow | The optimiser reports `overflow`; raise the pool's context floor or reduce `reserveOutputTokens` | | Config ignored | The file wins after first run; check `~/.config/omlx-router/config.json` and the drift warning in status | | Prices look stale | `/router pricing refresh` (or menu → Refresh prices) refetches the public tables | When in doubt, run `/router debug` (TUI) or `opencode-model-router debug` (CLI) and include its output in a bug report. It contains no prompt text and no credentials. ## Security The plugin ships source and one wasm binary into a user's editor, so the boundaries are explicit and checked: - **The core cannot reach the host.** `dist/core.wasm` has zero imports — no filesystem, network, or clock — and `unsafe` is denied everywhere except the C ABI boundary in `core/src/lib.rs`. - **Resources are bounded.** Memory is capped at 16 MiB (a runaway allocation traps instead of taking the host down), and requests over 1 MiB, pools over 1024 models, or transcripts over 5,000 messages are refused. A trap degrades to `skip`, never a broken turn. - **Nothing is a secret.** `bun run security` fails the build on secret-shaped strings anywhere in the tree or the published tarball, on credential-shaped files, and on any npm dependency — there are none on purpose. The `{env:NAME}` placeholders in `config.example.json` are the only credential form the router understands. - **CI** runs gitleaks over the full history and `cargo audit` against `core/Cargo.lock`; Dependabot watches the GitHub actions and the Rust crates. ## Development ```sh bun install bun run build:wasm # cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --release bun test # adapter + WASM bridge tests bun run test:rust # cargo test bun run check # fmt, clippy, tests, size gate, security gate bun run security # secret scan of the tree and the published tarball bun run test:e2e # live prompt tests against OpenCode + Kilo (needs a local judge) bun run test:e2e:live # one prompt through the real local judge bun run judge:calibrate # real judge verdicts + latency across six cases bun run routing:eval # real judge routing vs a ground-truth oracle bun run bench # deterministic routing/cost benchmark bun run bench:long # the same at 12k–208k context bun run quality:eval # live task-quality eval (spends provider tokens) ``` The prompt tests start real OpenCode/Kilo sessions, inject a deterministic judge, and assert both the decision record and the model each host actually used. See [tests/e2e/README.md](tests/e2e/README.md). The repository uses [jj](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj) on top of git (colocated). Conventional commits, `main` is the release bookmark. Layout: ```text core/ Rust decision engine (no I/O), compiled to dist/core.wasm src/ plain-JS host adapters, judge client, state, commands src/tui.js OpenCode TUI /router command + palette (plain JS) bin/ CLI (opencode-model-router, alias omlx-router) tests/ Bun tests and fixtures docs/ design spec and deeper docs ``` ## License Apache-2.0. # Changelog

## 0.2.8 — 2026-11-21

### Changed

- No code changes since 0.2.7. This release exists to validate the CI release
  pipeline: it is staged by GitHub Actions over npm trusted publishing (OIDC)
  and approved with 2FA, so it carries a signed provenance attestation
  (0.2.7 was published manually and has none). Behaviour is identical to
  0.2.7.

## 0.2.7 — 2026-11-21

### Added

- The incumbent is priced with the **measured** cache-hit share of the
  session's last turn (verified against recorded provider costs: cached tokens
  are reported apart from `input`, which covers only cache misses). A pin that
  has not served a turn yet is priced cold — it has earned no cache — and
  `pin.cacheHitRatio` (0.8) remains the fallback when nothing is measurable
  and the hard off switch at 0.
- `bun run judge:calibrate --repeat n` re-samples verdicts, pushes each one
  through the core's scoring, and stores the widest score-gap movement as a
  verdict-noise band. `pin.switchThreshold` is floored at that band, so a gap
  inside the judge's own spread cannot flip the model (the flip-flop turn
  guard stays). Measured on a local Qwen3-4B over 18 re-sampled verdicts:
  zero movement — the floor is a no-op for deterministic judges and matters
  for noisy ones.
- The benchmark reports now include two sensitivity sweeps over the cache-hit
  assumption (rescoring fixed decisions and re-running the router) and
  measured judge wall-clock next to the modelled dollars. The long suite
  crosses over: at 50% reuse switching every turn is 14% cheaper than keeping
  the incumbent, at 95% keeping is 9% cheaper, and the documented 80% default
  sits near the crossover — the two retention modes are cost-neutral there
  within the assumption's own sensitivity.

### Changed

- Every `/router` popup — menus and subcommands alike — is now labelled,
  aligned, wrapped text instead of long `·`-chained lines: section titles,
  a label column, one fact per row, and values wrapped under a hanging indent
  (`src/format.js`). The same layout renders in the OpenCode TUI, Kilo, and
  the CLI, and a regression test sweeps every popup asserting no line runs
  past 80 columns and that rows in a section share one value column.
- Model labels no longer show a `#default` variant suffix.

### Fixed

- Mutating a config object returned by `readConfig` (for example
  `config.judge.baseURL = ...`) no longer poisons the shared defaults for the
  rest of the process: `mergeConfig` deep-copies its base.
- Error alerts and download toasts wrap or clip instead of running past the
  popup width — long provisioning errors (like a missing oMLX admin key) were
  single 180-column lines.

## 0.2.6 — 2026-11-21

### Security

- `bun run security` and a CI job fail the build on secret-shaped strings in
  the tree or the published tarball, on credential-shaped files, and on any npm
  dependency (there are none on purpose). gitleaks scans the full history and
  `cargo audit` watches `core/Cargo.lock`; Dependabot tracks the GitHub actions
  and Rust crates.
- The wasm core's memory is capped at 16 MiB, `unsafe` is denied outside the
  C ABI boundary, and oversized requests (over 1 MiB), pools (over 1024
  models), and transcripts (over 5,000 messages) are refused. A core trap
  degrades to `skip` instead of failing the turn.

## 0.2.5 — 2026-11-19

- `/router retention [cache|balanced|switch]` renames `pin-mode`, which was

### Fixed

## 0.2.4 — 2026-11-18

### Fixed

- OpenCode V2 no longer downgrades to a smaller context window on the strength
  of a queued compaction. A later prompt verifies a completed checkpoint and
  checks that the active conversation fits before switching.

## 0.2.3 — 2026-11-18

### Added

- Pricing fallback: when the host catalog has no price, the router reads the
  public models.dev and LiteLLM tables (no access token) and caches them for 24

  `opencode-model-router pricing provider/model` manage the table; `pricing`

### Fixed

  models.dev's flat `{input, output, cache_read, cache_write}` with `tiers` and
  `context_over_200k`, and the V2 client's `{text: {input: {price}}}` with
  context overrides. A price the host leaves out stays missing, so the display
  says `unknown` instead of `$0`, and a real zero still reads as free.

## 0.2.0 — 2026-11-17

### Added

- Custom policy weights: `policyWeights` overrides any preset, and
  `policyByClass` varies the blend by turn class (`planning`, `review`,
  `trivial`, and so on). `/router policy custom` prints the active weights.
  The benchmark adds a mixed-weight scenario.
- Local models are first-class pool members: `pool.localCostZero` prices
  loopback providers at zero, and free local models get size-based quality
  (under 3B 0.35, 3–8B 0.45, 8–30B 0.55, 30B+ 0.72). The benchmark includes a
  local 27B and 4B. A free adequate model now releases a paid incumbent.
- Quality scores come from public datasets by default, keyless and cached
  daily: Epoch AI (SWE-bench Verified or MirrorCode, then ECI) followed by the
  LMArena Code Arena. `quality.sources` sets the priority, `quality.overrides`
  still win, and unmatched models keep the heuristic. `/router quality` and
  `omlx-router quality` show per-source counts and age; `refresh` fetches both.
- `judge.provision.backend` (`auto` | `omlx` | `none`): llama.cpp and other
  OpenAI-compatible judge servers are detected, and the download commands print
  a setup recipe instead of failing on the oMLX admin API.
- Failover on provider failures: a 429, 5xx, timeout, or auth error blocks the
  model for a cooldown, clears the pin, and queues a same-turn redirect to the
  next candidate through OpenCode's `model.resolve` hook. Config under
  `failover`; the blocklist shows in `/router debug`.
- `bun run quality:eval`: eight verifiable coding tasks run through OpenCode
  with fixed models, graded by deterministic checks. Results live in
  `docs/benchmarks/`.
- `bun run bench`: a deterministic routing and cost benchmark over a ten-turn
  session, comparing fixed models, a simulated tier baseline, and the router in
  `cache`, `balanced`, and `switch` modes. `bun run bench:long` repeats it from
  12k to 208k context. Results live in `docs/benchmarks/`.
- `/router version` and `omlx-router version --json`: router version, host, ABI,
  and wasm path for scripts and bug reports.
- `/router debug` and `omlx-router debug [--json]`: read-only diagnostics with a
  secret-free config digest, catalog/judge health, pins, last decision, and turn
  timing. Available from the TUI menu as **Diagnostics**.

### Changed

- Package renamed to `@231self/opencode-router`. The CLI installs as
  `opencode-model-router`, with `omlx-router` kept as an alias. Plugin IDs,
  config/state paths, and `OMLX_ROUTER_*` env vars are unchanged.
- The README now leads with a "How it works" section covering the judge prompt
  and floor, deterministic signals, gates and scoring, pin modes, the context
  optimiser, the three cache layers, and subagent policy, with npm/CI/license
  badges and a quick start.

### Fixed

- A pinned model that leaves the pool (context gate, catalog change) now hands
  over to an adequate candidate instead of the highest scorer.
- Context size no longer raises complexity at all. The context gate and the
  optimiser handle capacity, so routine edits at 10–200k stay on smaller
  models instead of being routed to the frontier model.
- Near-miss models (shortfall within `limits.shortfallTolerance`) now compete
  only when no exact-adequate candidate exists. The tolerance is a starvation
  fallback, not a licence to under-route.
- A free adequate model can now release a paid incumbent; the cost-release
  filter previously skipped zero-cost candidates.
- A pin no longer holds an inadequate model when complexity rises gradually. The
  +2 jump rule missed a 1→2→3 climb, so a cheap incumbent could stay above the
  turn's required quality; it now releases with reason `quality-gate` and
  selects the best adequate candidate.

## 0.1.2 — 2026-11-16

### Added

- `pin.mode`: `cache` (sticky), `balanced` (default), or `switch` (best every
  turn, cold-cache scoring). `/router pin-mode` and the Pin mode menu item

- `/router explain` is a readable breakdown (policy, verdict, judge time, top
  scores, per-turn cost), and `/router pool` shows each model's cost.

### Fixed

- Pins release after `pin.maxTurns` (8) or `pin.maxAgeMs` (30 min) even while
  active. A model costing more than `pin.costSwitchRatio` (4×) the cheapest
  adequate challenger is replaced even if it has the higher score, because one
  cache miss is cheaper than keeping an overpriced incumbent indefinitely.

## 0.1.0 — 2026-11-16

First release.

### Added

- Per-turn routing for OpenCode V2, with same-turn model switching from the
  prompt hook.
- Deterministic Rust/WASM decision core: turn envelope, triage, scoring,
  cache-aware pinning, optimiser planning.
- oMLX small-model judge with automatic smallest-model selection, 5 s default
  timeout, LRU verdict cache, repair retry, and deterministic fallback.
- Judge provisioning with explicit consent: TUI/CLI offer, model metadata and
  size before confirmation, oMLX admin download, progress, cancel, and
  post-download verification. Never downloads automatically.
- Live prompt tests (`tests/e2e`) for OpenCode V2 and Kilo: deterministic judge
  stub, multi-turn pin/threshold/jump/override scenarios, subagent policy,
  judge failure and malformed-output fallbacks, disabled mode, Kilo boundary
  semantics, and a real-oMLX judge smoke test. Each step asserts the decision
  record, the model the host actually used, and per-turn timing.
- Per-turn telemetry from host events: routing, local judge, remote model,
  tool/other, time to first token, steps, tokens, and cost. `/router timing`,
  `omlx-router timing`, and `/router status` show the split; records are
  `turns.jsonl` with no prompt text.
- `tests/judge-calibration.mjs` measures the real judge's verdicts and latency
  on simple/edit/debug/planning/review/large-context cases.
- Pool sources: host favorites (default), explicit list, all available models;
  include/exclude globs; tool, context, and status filters; local-model guard.
- Policies: cost-first (default), quality-first, latency-first, with per-agent
  overrides for all of them.
- Cache-aware pinning with switch threshold, idle TTL, flip-flop guard, user
  `/model` override detection, compaction reset, and per-session tool-failure
  escalation.
- Context optimiser: dedupe, truncate, stub stale tool outputs, protect system
  and user text, overflow hand-off to host compaction.
- Subagent routing: role detection, agent policies, explicit agent-model forced
  pins, parent-model tie-break, independent pins and escalation.
- OpenCode TUI `/router` command and palette entry: status, on/off, interactive
  policy picker, pool, history, timing, explain, pin/auto, judge probe,
  subagents.
- Kilo V1 shim: routes at the next request boundary through the SDK transport,
  best-effort optimiser transform, boundary-labelled decisions.
- `omlx-router` CLI: status, config get/set, history, timing, doctor, pool.
- Apache-2.0 license, CI (rustfmt, clippy, Rust tests, wasm build, Bun tests,
  wasm size gate), and user documentation.

### Fixed

- The 4B judge copied the schema's `complexity: 1` example and under-classified
  debug, review, and planning turns. The judge prompt now uses few-shot examples
  and an explicit "do not copy" rule; the core also raises the judge verdict to
  a deterministic floor from code, error, planning, review, and context signals.
- Marker matching now uses word boundaries and common inflections, so `Inspect`
  no longer matches `spec`, `prefix` no longer matches `fix`, and `designs` /
  `tests` still match their markers.
- Multi-file turns now set a `multiFile` signal; planning and review turns have
  a minimum complexity of 3. The routing eval found two under-routes (a
  three-file refactor and a design comparison) before this change; both now
  match the oracle.
- The default judge timeout is 5 s: the 4B is usually under 1 s but cold calls
  measured 3.4 s.

- The OpenCode V2 context hook only reports a model's provider and id. The
  adapter now fills in limits from the live catalog, so the optimiser no longer
  sees zero context and reports a false overflow on every turn.
- Context-hook state writes no longer overwrite a routing pin written by a
  concurrent prompt hook. Cache-aware pinning now survives turns with tool use.
- Pin policy: a downward complexity change no longer counts as a jump, a
  selection that stays on the incumbent is no longer recorded as a switch, and
  idle TTL only switches when a different model is actually best.
- A rejected `switchModel` call is recorded with `applied: "none"` and the
  error, instead of claiming the decision was applied.

### Notes

- No TypeScript application code; no Python runtime.
- Kilo cannot switch the in-flight turn through its V1 API; decisions apply at
  the next boundary.
